senses.definition: (medicine) Dealing with the practical management of patients, in practice at the point of care; as contrasted with other health care venues (see clinical medicine for more explanation).

quotes.text: “We are social beings,” Jaime Blandino, a clinical psychologist in Decatur, Georgia, told CNN. “My most extroverted clients are having the hardest time.”
quotes.reference: 2020 March 23, Ryan Prior, “The extrovert’s guide to social distancing”, in CNN:

senses.definition: Of or pertaining to a clinic, such as a medical clinic or law clinic.
examples: Medicine is now more often practiced in a clinical setting than in the home.

senses.definition: Cool and emotionless, in a professional way, as contrasted with an impetuous or unprofessional way.

examples: We took a clinical approach to resolving conflicts.

quotes.text: Fly-half Jonny Wilkinson put his below-par performance against Argentina behind him with a fine first-half showing, slotting four kicks from six and controlling his back-line with aplomb, while England's three-quarters were brimming with life and clinical with their execution.
quotes.reference: 2011 September 24, Ben Dirs, “Rugby World Cup 2011: England 67-3 Romania”, in BBC Sport:

quotes.text: Remarkably United’s 10 men almost salvaged an improbable draw during a late, spirited challenge. They showed great competitive courage in that period and there were chances for Robin van Persie, Ángel Di María and Marouane Fellaini to punish City for defending too deeply and not being more clinical with their opportunities at the other end.
quotes.reference: 2014 November 2, Daniel Taylor, “Sergio Agüero strike wins derby for Manchester City against 10-man United”, in The Guardian:

quotes.text: Jones was insanely productive last season. He is a clinical route-runner who can line up at any position and catches everything.

senses.definition: (obsolete) Of or relating to a bed, especially a deathbed.
examples: a clinical convert: one who turns to religion on their death-bed

senses.definition: (education) A medical student's session spent in a real-world nursing environment.
